sections.content_markdown: Again, collect the data of cooling the water vapor and set them on a graph sheet with X axis telling time and Y axis telling temperature. It will be like fig 2.10.

The graph shows the initial temperature of water vapor is $140^\circ\text{C}$. When in the process of cooling it to $100^\circ\text{C}$, the vapor starts to turn into water. It remains $100^\circ\text{C}$ until all the vapor is turned into water. Further cooling starts to decrease the temperature of water. When it reaches $0^\circ\text{C}$, the water starts to transform into ice. It remains the same until all the water is turned into ice and then the temperature of ice decreases from $0^\circ\text{C}$. The fig 2.10 shows a decrease of temperature of ice to $-40^\circ\text{C}$.

figures.caption: Fig 2.10: Cooling curve of vapor.
figures.description: A line graph showing the temperature of water as it cools over time from vapor at 140 degrees Celsius, condensing to liquid water at 100 degrees Celsius, cooling to 0 degrees Celsius, freezing to ice, and further cooling to -40 degrees Celsius.
